title: The war in Ukraine explained
subtitle: Since February 24, 2022
subject: comprendreLeMonde
description: An invasion supposed to last three days became the biggest war in Europe since 1945. A look back at the causes and consequences of the conflict in **Ukraine**.

hero.hook: A lightning offensive meant to last three days turned into the biggest war in Europe since 1945.

blocks.text: On February 24, 2022, Russia launched a massive military offensive against **Ukraine**, triggering the most devastating conflict on European soil since 1945. This event is not sudden: it is the culmination of tensions accumulated over decades around Ukrainian sovereignty.

sections.title: Post-Soviet heritage and the clash of identities

blocks.text: The roots of the war lie in the dislocation of the USSR in 1991. The independence of Ukraine is experienced by some of the Russian elites, including Vladimir Putin, as an amputation of the historic heart of Russia, who refuse to see it as a fully sovereign nation.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky lent his voice to Paddington Bear in the Ukrainian version of the film, a nod to his acting career before politics.

Ukraine, which had the world's third largest nuclear arsenal in 1991, chose to disarm. Through the **[[The Budapest Memorandum (1994)]]**, it exchanges its warheads for guarantees of territorial integrity. But its rapprochement with the EU and NATO is seen by the Kremlin as a hostile encirclement.

The definitive break came in 2014, when the Ukrainian people ousted a pro-Russian president during the Maidan revolution. In response, Russia illegally annexes Crimea and supports a separatist insurgency in : a conflict frozen for eight years that will serve as a laboratory for all-out war in 2022. **[[Donbass]]**

On February 24, 2022, the Russian army launched its offensive on several fronts. Moscow's objective is to overthrow the Kyiv government in a few days, an ambition which is based on a major error: the underestimation of Ukrainian national cohesion and the modernization of its army since 2014.

blocks.caption: The Russian invasion of February 2022 caused significant destruction in many Ukrainian cities.

blocks.text: President Volodymyr Zelensky refuses US-proposed evacuation, saying: "I need ammunition, not a taxi." Through his daily messages, he becomes the symbol of a nation that refuses to give in.

The battle of Kyiv ended in a bitter Russian failure in the spring of 2022. Faced with mobile Ukrainian resistance using Western weapons, Moscow withdrew its troops from the north to concentrate on the east and the south: the conflict descended into a war of attrition, with a front line of more than 1,000 kilometers.

sections.title: A global economic and security earthquake

blocks.text: The shock wave of the invasion extends beyond the Ukrainian borders. Western powers are deploying an unprecedented arsenal of sanctions to paralyze the Russian war machine: the exclusion of Russian banks from the **[[SWIFT]]** system and the freezing of central bank reserves mark a historic break. These measures also disrupt energy flows, with Europe having to initiate a rapid transition away from Russian gas, on which it was 40% dependent.
At the start of the conflict, the Ukrainian government updated its “Diia” app to allow citizens to report the position of Russian tanks in real time.

The agricultural sector is the other big victim: Ukraine, nicknamed “the breadbasket of Europe”, sees its ports blocked, threatening countries dependent on its cereals with famine. The conflict also united the Atlantic Alliance, pushing Finland and Sweden to join NATO.

After more than two years of fighting, the war became a high-intensity conflict where drones and satellites rub shoulders with trench methods from another century. The failure of the Ukrainian counter-offensives in 2023 shows that the terrain has become very difficult to reconquer, between minefields and constant surveillance of the battlefield.

blocks.caption: Western military support for Ukraine, via NATO, has intensified throughout the conflict.

blocks.text: The issue becomes one of industrial endurance: Russia has shifted its economy towards a model of total war, while Ukraine depends on the continuity of Western military and financial aid.

blocks.text: Ukrainian resistance has turned a lightning invasion meant to last three days into a global war of attrition that has redefined Cold War alliances and upended global energy and food security.
